newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA TO CRACKDOWN ON CORRUPTION WITHIN POLICE.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA TO CRACKDOWN ON CORRUPTION WITHIN POLICE.

text.p: Bulgaria's police said on Tuesday it would boost measures to combat corruption within their ranks and white-collar crime in the country by employing highly qualified young economists.
"This year police has filed six suits against police officers on suspicion in corruption and another 18 officers were investigated," National Police director Slavcho Bosilkov told a news conference.
Last year 38 police officers have been investigated for corruption and one suit has been filed, he said.
Crime and corruption have flourished in the country in the seven years since the collapse of communism and poorly-paid and ill-equipped police are vulnarable to corruption.

"It is obvious that the only effective way to fight white collar crime is to have young experts in economy, law and computer technologies in the Economic Police Directorate and the National Investigation Service," Bosilkov said.
He said five experts from the FBI will arrive on Wednesday to provide technical assistance to the Bulgarian police officers in cracking down tax evasion and misappropriation of funds.
Bulgaria's police caught the perpetrators of more than 4,000 economic crimes accounting for some 30.6 billion levs ($19 million) in the first four months of the year, police said.
